subject: System Design
title: Document Databases
description: A micro-lesson that makes Document Databases usable.

hook.text: In MongoDB, a user document contains their profile, addresses, and orders — all in one JSON object.

buildup.text: Document databases store data as flexible JSON-like documents instead of rigid rows in tables.

discovery.text: No schema migration needed. Each document can have different fields. Fast iteration for startups.

twist.text: Without a schema, bad data creeps in silently. A typo in a field name goes undetected for months.

climax.text: Document databases trade schema enforcement for flexibility. Great for evolving data models, risky for data quality.

punchline.text: Flexible documents, but you own the data quality.

quiz.question: What is a key advantage of document databases?
options: Flexible schemas that don't require migrations
